rows.label: lukewarm
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve lacking enthusiasm and investment, but lukewarm is half-hearted participation while apathetic is a deeper indifference to outcomes and people, with minimal effort.
rows.opus_reason: Apathetic is the same lack of engagement as lukewarm, carried further into not caring at all and putting in minimal effort.

rows.label: severe
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve holding people to high standards without leniency, but severe adds a stern, unsmiling manner and harsh judgment, while strict stresses demanding results and a belief in growth through pushing.
rows.opus_reason: Both centre on holding people to strict standards without leniency. Severe adds a stern, unsmiling manner and harsh criticism, while strict adds a results-driven philosophy of pushing people to grow, so they overlap heavily but differ in emphasis.

rows.label: quick-tempered
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe flaring up quickly at small provocations before cooling down, so they are essentially the same concept, with irascible perhaps slightly stronger (anger, barking).

rows.label: genteel
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve courteous manners, but genteel adds refined breeding and avoiding crudeness in dress and conduct, while polite is basic civility; one can be polite without being refined.
rows.opus_reason: Genteel is basic politeness carried further, adding refinement and good-breeding standards in dress and conduct, so it encompasses polite courtesy with greater scope.

rows.label: undependable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe failing to follow through on commitments so that others cannot count on the person; the labels are near-synonyms and could replace each other.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe failing to follow through on promises and commitments so others cannot count on one; the labels are interchangeable synonyms.

rows.label: resolved
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve steadfastly pursuing a goal despite obstacles, but resolved stresses steadiness of purpose against doubt and pressure, while persevering stresses continued effort through failure and setbacks until completion.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean sticking to a goal despite obstacles. Resolved stresses firmness of will against doubt and pressure, while persevering stresses repeated effort over time through setbacks, so they differ only in emphasis.

rows.label: dissocial
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe choosing solitude and keeping apart from others rather than seeking company, so they are essentially the same concept, with solitary just spelling out more behaviors.

rows.label: sensing
rows.sonnet_reason: Both are about noticing subtle cues and shifts in the room, but 'sensing' is broader (any surroundings) and includes acting on the cues, while 'socially-perceptive' is specifically about social and emotional cues.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe picking up subtle cues in the room; socially-perceptive narrows this to social signals, while sensing is broader and adds acting on the cues.

rows.label: undespondent
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve keeping a light, good-spirited outlook even in bad times, but 'undespondent' is specifically resilience through setbacks, while 'cheerful' is a broader disposition that includes brightening at small things and noticing the positive.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a light-hearted good cheer. Undespondent narrows it to holding up through setbacks, while cheerful is the general everyday disposition, so they differ mainly in scope.

rows.label: faulty
rows.sonnet_reason: Both cover defective, unreliable work from lack of skill, but 'faulty' also includes character flaws and poor judgment, while 'incompetent' is specifically about lacking the know-how to do the job.
rows.opus_reason: Incompetent covers the skill-and-work side of faulty, while faulty is broader and also takes in flaws of character and conduct, so they differ mainly in scope.

rows.label: uncareful
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe rough, unchecked work that lets small errors slide; sloppy adds a slightly more visible messy output but is essentially the same concept.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe working without care, skipping checks and leaving small errors; sloppy adds a little emphasis on rough, visibly messy output and haste, but the concept is essentially the same.

rows.label: strange
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe peculiar, unconventional behavior and indifference to being seen as odd; eccentric adds a more specific emphasis on following one's own template and puzzlement at convention.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe unconventional, odd behaviour coupled with indifference to being seen as odd. Eccentric adds only a shade of puzzlement at conventional ways.

rows.label: craven
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe shrinking from danger or confrontation out of fear when courage is called for; they are near-synonyms, with cowardly slightly stressing leaving others to face it.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe giving in to fear and avoiding danger or confrontation when courage is called for; craven and cowardly are interchangeable.

rows.label: worriless
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe calm, unanxious handling of setbacks without rehearsing trouble, but 'worriless' centers on absence of anxiety about the future while 'composed' adds outward poise (level voice, no nervous energy).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe an unanxious calm that doesn't dwell on future trouble; composed puts more weight on outward steadiness of manner, worriless on the inner absence of worry.

rows.label: screwy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe an openly odd, unconventional person who doesn't hide it, though 'screwy' adds unpredictability and a hint of craziness while 'eccentric' stresses indifference to convention.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe openly odd, unconventional behaviour, but screwy adds unpredictability and a hint of craziness that goes beyond plain eccentricity.

rows.label: nonirritable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve emotional steadiness, but nonirritable is specifically about patience and not getting annoyed by frustrations, while even-tempered is about consistent mood across good and bad, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe calm composure under frustration; even-tempered is the broader mood stability that largely includes not being irritable, a difference of scope.

rows.label: unsanitary
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe habitual uncleanliness of person and home, with unwashed dishes and indifference to grime; slovenly adds a sense of general untidiness and unkemptness, while unsanitary stresses germs and hygiene.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe habitually letting oneself and one's home go dirty and not minding the grime, so either label could stand in for the other.

rows.label: munificent
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe freely giving resources to benefit others; munificent is a more lavish, grander degree of the same generosity.
rows.opus_reason: Munificent is generosity carried to a lavish, grand degree; it is the same concept with more intensity.

rows.label: conforming
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe going along with prevailing norms and not challenging convention; 'conforming' stresses behavior and manners, while 'conformist' stresses opinions and beliefs, so the scope differs slightly.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe going along with what is conventional; one stresses customary behaviour and the other mainstream opinions, so they differ only in emphasis.

rows.label: flirtatious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe playful romantic banter that signals interest; 'flirty' is just a more casual synonym of 'flirtatious', with perhaps slightly more emphasis on seductive or sexual tension.

rows.label: stinging
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe speaking with a cutting, biting edge that stings; acerbic adds acidic wit and a criticism focus, but the core is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe cutting, biting speech that stings. Acerbic differs only in emphasis, adding acidic wit and a critical bent.

rows.label: pacifistic
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a principled, consistent opposition to war and violence in all circumstances, differing only in wording and slight emphasis (refusing arms vs. advocating alternatives).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe principled opposition to violence and war in all circumstances; the labels are interchangeable.

rows.label: contemplative
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve calm, quiet, inward reflection, but 'meditative' adds mindfulness and present-moment awareness and a peaceful tone that guides others, while 'contemplative' stresses slow, thoughtful turning over of questions and preferring stillness to activity.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe quiet, reflective inward attention and stillness; meditative adds a mindfulness and present-moment emphasis but is essentially the same concept.

rows.label: philosophizing
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a disposition to reflect on fundamental questions of existence, knowledge and value; 'philosophical' is slightly broader in wording but the concept is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe reflecting on fundamental questions of reality, knowledge, and value; 'philosophical' is slightly broader in scope (deeper meanings, abstract concepts) while 'philosophizing' emphasizes repeated careful reasoning.

rows.label: boorish
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe habitually impolite, ill-mannered behavior toward others; boorish stresses a settled habit and coarse disregard, while rude is the broader, more general term with concrete examples.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe habitual discourtesy and ill manners toward others; boorish frames it as a settled disregard for others' feelings, while rude lists specific lapses in courtesy, so they differ only in emphasis.

rows.label: fussy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve exacting standards and attention to detail, but fussy stresses being hard to please and rejecting shortfalls over small things, while perfectionist stresses flawless, exhaustive quality in one's own work, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe exacting standards and close attention to detail; perfectionist carries this further, toward flawlessness and completeness throughout, while fussy stresses being hard to satisfy about small things.

rows.label: unemotional
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe keeping emotional distance and staying composed; dispassionate adds objectivity and neutrality, while unemotional stresses not being stirred by feelings, so they are near-synonyms with slightly different emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean keeping emotions at a distance, but dispassionate puts more weight on objectivity and neutrality in judgment and discussion, while unemotional stresses not being stirred by feelings.

rows.label: unconciliatory
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe refusing to give ground or compromise in a dispute; 'unyielding' emphasizes firmness under pressure while 'unconciliatory' emphasizes refusing to make peace, which is a slight difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe holding one's position firmly in a dispute and refusing to give ground or concede for peace, so the two labels are interchangeable.

rows.label: acid
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe speaking with a cutting, biting, stinging edge; 'acerbic' adds wit and a critical tone, but the core concept is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe sharp, stinging, biting speech; acerbic adds a slight emphasis on witty criticism, while acid stresses corrosive wearing-down.

rows.label: mundane
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe plain, unflamboyant style, but mundane covers any workaday manner while prosaic specifically stresses matter-of-fact, unpoetic expression, so they share a core with different emphases.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a plain manner with no flair. Prosaic is the narrower case, limited to matter-of-fact, unpoetic expression, while mundane covers how one handles everything.

rows.label: mild-hearted
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a mild, kind, non-harsh manner toward people; mild-hearted adds easy forgiveness and patience, while gentle emphasizes softness in delivery and restraint from cutting replies, so they are nearly the same concept with slightly different emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe mild, soft, non-harsh treatment of others, patience with faults, and kindness in place of severity, so they are essentially the same concept.

rows.label: purposeless
rows.sonnet_reason: Languishing includes living without purpose and drifting through days, which is the core of purposeless, but it also adds stagnation, social disconnection and emptiness, so each has something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Languishing explicitly includes living without purpose and drifting through the days, adding hollowness and decline on top, so it is a broader version of purposelessness.

rows.label: picky
rows.sonnet_reason: Picky-eater is a food-specific form of rejecting options, but it stems from familiarity and aversion to the unfamiliar rather than high standards for getting things just right, so they overlap without either implying the other.
rows.opus_reason: Picky-eater is pickiness narrowed to food, with an added fear of the unfamiliar, so it is the same concept in a narrower scope.

rows.label: incongenial
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe being hard to get along with, but 'disagreeable' here stresses contradicting people and disregarding harmony, while 'incongenial' is a broader unpleasant disposition that repels others, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe an unpleasant disposition that makes a person hard to be around. Disagreeable is the narrower, confrontational form of it, adding contradiction and indifference to keeping the peace.

rows.label: unsurprising
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve adhering to the expected, standard way, but 'unsurprising' emphasizes predictability to others while 'conventional' emphasizes preference for standard approaches and distrust of originality; each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both centre on sticking to conventional, expected ways. Unsurprising stresses being predictable to others, while conventional stresses preferring standard templates over originality.

rows.label: unneurotic
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe emotional steadiness, but unneurotic centers on not fretting or panicking over setbacks and uncertainty, while even-tempered centers on consistent mood across good and bad days; they overlap without either implying the other.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe emotional steadiness when setbacks or news arrive; unneurotic stresses freedom from worry and panic, while even-tempered stresses an unchanging mood, so they are the same stability with a different emphasis.

rows.label: convivial
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe enjoying and seeking out company, but convivial adds warmth, good humor, and festive geniality, while gregarious stresses outgoing sociability, so they are nearly the same with a slight difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe actively seeking and enjoying others' company. Convivial adds warmth and festive good humor, so the two differ only in emphasis.

rows.label: light-minded
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve treating things lightly with jokes and breeziness, but light-minded specifically means dismissing serious matters, whereas lighthearted is a general cheerful, easy disposition that need not be dismissive.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe bringing jokey, easy lightness to weighty matters; light-minded is the narrower, more pejorative focus on dismissing serious things, while lighthearted is the broader general disposition.

rows.label: easeless
rows.sonnet_reason: Both centre on habitual restless unease, but 'anxious' adds anticipating things going wrong while 'easeless' stresses inability to rest, so each has content the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe habitual unease and restless tension. Easeless stresses a constant inability to settle, while anxious stresses worry about things going wrong, so they differ mainly in emphasis.

rows.label: perspicacious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve sharp perception of people and situations, but perspicacious is broader (any details, hidden motives) while socially-perceptive is limited to social cues and mood.
rows.opus_reason: Social perceptiveness is a narrower form of perspicacity, reading people and rooms, without its broader insight into details and hidden motives in all situations.

rows.label: oversuspicious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe excessive, unfounded suspicion of others' motives; paranoid adds a stronger emphasis on perceived threats and conspiracies, so it is the same concept differing mainly in degree.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe excessive, unwarranted suspicion of others' motives; paranoid carries it further, to imagined threats and conspiracies and distrust of institutions.

rows.label: trusty
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe keeping commitments without reminders and being someone others can rely on, so the descriptions are nearly identical in meaning.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe reliably following through on commitments so others can count on one's word, and either label could replace the other.

rows.label: heroic
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve facing danger to protect others, but heroic stresses self-sacrifice and rescue without hesitation, while brave stresses acting despite fear, including in confrontations; each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both are about facing danger for something worth protecting, and heroic is essentially bravery taken further into self-sacrifice to protect or rescue others.

rows.label: elegiac
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve habitual sadness, but elegiac is a wistful, soft focus on loss and the past, while melancholic is brooding sadness and negativity in general; each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Elegiac is a specific form of habitual melancholy, focused wistfully on loss and the past, so it is a narrower version of the melancholic disposition.

rows.label: hearty
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve warm, welcoming manner, but hearty adds booming, expansive, generous exuberance regardless of mood, while friendly is general goodwill and approachability without that intensity.
rows.opus_reason: Hearty is friendliness carried to a booming, expansive, effusive degree, so it is the same warm goodwill with more volume and exuberance.

rows.label: thickheaded
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe being slow to grasp things and needing repeated explanation, with slow-witted adding slow replies and thickheaded adding persistent missing of the point; essentially the same concept with slight emphasis differences.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe slowness in grasping things and needing repeated explanation; the differences are only slight emphasis (thickheaded stresses missing the point entirely, slow-witted adds belated retorts).

rows.label: mothering
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve warm, patient caring and gentle guidance, but mothering adds self-sacrifice and protectiveness in a maternal mode, while nurturing emphasizes fostering growth, so they are very close but differ in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe warm, caring support with gentle guidance; mothering is a more protective, self-sacrificing, maternal form of nurturing.

rows.label: grandiloquent
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe inflated, pompous, grandiose speech meant to impress; bombastic stresses overwhelming the listener a bit more, while grandiloquent stresses elaborate lofty diction, but they are nearly interchangeable.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe inflated, pompous, grandiose language used for lofty effect, and either label could stand in for the other.

rows.label: embittered
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a sour, resentful, cynical outlook shaped by past grievances and disappointments; 'bitter' is nearly the same concept, with embittered stressing the process and added suspicion.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a sour, resentful, cynical outlook shaped by past grievances and disappointments, essentially interchangeable.

rows.label: unspiritual
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve lacking religious orientation, but unspiritual is personal disinterest in the sacred, while secular is a method of reasoning that relies on empirical and naturalistic grounds; each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe setting religion aside in how one thinks; secular stresses reasoning by empirical, naturalistic methods, while unspiritual stresses personal indifference to the sacred.

rows.label: stuffy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve formal, non-casual manner, but stuffy adds rigid conventionality and discomfort with relaxed behavior across all dealings, while formal is just a proper, dignified register of language suited to the context.
rows.opus_reason: Stuffy is formality carried to an extreme: rigid, applied in every setting, and uneasy with casualness, whereas formal is a professional register suited to the context.

rows.label: unadaptable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both favor established methods over new ones, but 'traditional' is a preference for time-tested approaches, while 'unadaptable' is rigid insistence on old ways despite changed circumstances; each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both favour established ways over new ones, but unadaptable takes this preference to a rigid refusal to adjust whatever changes, which is a matter of degree.

rows.label: good enough
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve accepting one's own work and conduct as adequate and letting shortfalls go; self-accepting adds resilience to others' opinions and acknowledging flaws, while good enough adds not striving for excellence.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean accepting one's own work and conduct as adequate and not dwelling on flaws; 'good enough' is the narrower form, adding contentment with being ordinary rather than striving for excellence.

rows.label: hidebound
rows.sonnet_reason: Both prefer established ways over new ones, but hidebound adds rigid refusal to consider change, while traditional is a milder preference that can still weigh alternatives.
rows.opus_reason: Both favour established ways over new ones, and hidebound is the more rigid degree, refusing change outright rather than merely preferring the familiar.

rows.label: well-to-do
rows.sonnet_reason: Both mean being rich and prosperous; 'wealthy' is described with more specific detail about lifestyle and extent, but it is essentially the same concept.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe being rich and prosperous; the wealthy description just elaborates the same condition.

rows.label: laughterless
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a settled grave, serious disposition with little humor; solemn adds formality and dignity, while laughterless centers on the absence of laughter.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a settled grave, serious disposition. Laughterless stresses the absence of laughter, while solemn stresses dignity and formality, so they differ mainly in emphasis.

rows.label: passionless
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve emotional detachment and an unmoved manner, but dispassionate emphasizes objectivity and neutrality while passionless emphasizes lack of warmth and enthusiasm, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe emotional detachment and an unmoved manner. Dispassionate leans toward objectivity and neutrality, while passionless leans toward a lack of warmth and enthusiasm, so they differ mainly in emphasis.

rows.label: weak-hearted
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe shrinking from danger and confrontation out of fear; cowardly adds leaving others to face it, but the core is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe shrinking from danger and confrontation out of lack of courage. Cowardly adds a stronger, more pejorative emphasis on leaving others to face it, so the two differ mainly in degree.

rows.label: genial
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe warm, welcoming goodwill toward everyone in conversation; genial adds readily smiling and kind joking, while friendly is the broader general goodwill.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe warm, glad-to-talk goodwill toward everyone; genial adds a cheerful, joking, pleasant manner, while friendly stresses goodwill and being on someone's side, so they nearly coincide with a slight difference in emphasis.

rows.label: untidy
rows.sonnet_reason: Careless (Big Five) includes leaving things in a mess, which is the core of untidy, but it also covers lateness, rule-bending, low effort and giving up on hard tasks, so it is broader and neither implies the other.
rows.opus_reason: Careless is the broad low-conscientiousness trait, and leaving things in a mess is one of its parts, so untidy is a narrower facet of it.

rows.label: overtrusting
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve extending trust and believing others' intentions, but 'overtrusting' is the excessive, uncritical extreme (even without reason), while 'trusting' is a milder default expectation of decency until shown otherwise.
rows.opus_reason: Overtrusting is trusting carried to excess: trust extended even without grounds, with no checking.

rows.label: ultraspiritual
rows.sonnet_reason: Both prioritize the spiritual over the material, but 'ultraspiritual' is the more extreme, all-encompassing form of the same orientation that 'spiritual' describes.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe valuing the sacred and mystical above material things, and ultraspiritual is the same orientation carried to a greater degree.

rows.label: asinine
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe poor judgment and failing to learn from experience, but asinine stresses witless obtuseness and missing obvious points, while foolish adds failing to foresee consequences and giving misleading advice; they are near-synonyms differing in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe poor judgment that misses what matters and fails to learn from experience; asinine stresses witless obtuseness more strongly, while foolish adds poor foresight and bad advice.

rows.label: consoling
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve warmth toward people in pain, but consoling is the specific act of steadily comforting the grieving without rushing them, while compassionate is a broader empathic disposition that need not involve that comforting behavior.
rows.opus_reason: Consoling is a narrower, behavioural form of compassion: warm, patient comfort given to people in distress, where compassion is the broader empathic care for others' suffering.

rows.label: refined
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve courteous social conduct, but refined adds graceful bearing and cultivated elegance, while polite is basic civility that needs no polish or poise.
rows.opus_reason: Refined contains politeness but carries it further into cultivated grace, poise and elegance, so it is essentially polite manners raised to a higher degree.

rows.label: valiant
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe facing danger despite fear for a worthy cause; valiant is a bit more heroic and emphatic, but the core concept is the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe facing danger despite fear and pressing on for something worth protecting or believed right, and the two words are effectively synonyms.

rows.label: nonvolatile
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe staying composed and even under pressure or provocation; nonvolatile stresses not flaring into anger, unflappable stresses not being flustered by surprises, so they are nearly the same with a slight difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe staying even and composed under pressure; nonvolatile stresses not flaring into anger, while unflappable stresses not getting flustered, which is a difference of emphasis only.

rows.label: unpunctual
rows.sonnet_reason: Careless is a broad low-conscientiousness trait that includes showing up late, but also mess, rule-bending and giving up on tasks; unpunctual is only the lateness part, so they overlap without either implying the other.
rows.opus_reason: Careless is a broad low-conscientiousness trait whose description includes showing up late, so unpunctuality is a narrower part of it.

rows.label: condemning
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve harshly judging others' conduct negatively; 'condemning' stresses outspoken denouncing, while 'judgmental' stresses quick, one-sided opinion formation, so they are nearly the same with a slight difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe harsh negative judgment of others' conduct; condemning stresses openly denouncing it, while judgmental stresses quickly forming such opinions.

rows.label: thoroughgoing
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe thorough, careful attention to every detail, though meticulous stresses precision and accuracy while thoroughgoing stresses completeness and not skipping steps.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe complete, careful attention to every detail. Thoroughgoing stresses completeness and skipping no steps, while meticulous stresses precision; the core is shared and the difference is only emphasis.

rows.label: bilious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a short temper that snaps at small irritations; bilious adds a persistent sour, hard-to-shake crossness, while irascible stresses quick flaring anger and barking before thinking.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a short temper that snaps at small irritations; bilious adds a lingering sour crossness, while irascible stresses quick flare-ups, a difference of emphasis.

rows.label: unusual
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe acting on one's own odd notions rather than convention, and the target's description even uses 'eccentric'; the other adds indifference to appearances and puzzlement at conformity, a slight emphasis difference.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe following one's own odd ways rather than convention; eccentric adds only indifference to appearances and puzzlement at the usual way, a slight shift in emphasis.

rows.label: unvigorous
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe slow movement, low energy, and tiredness out of proportion to effort, so they are nearly the same concept, with only slight differences in emphasis (flat tone vs. dragging pace).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe low physical energy, slow movement and speech, and tiring easily; they differ only slightly in emphasis.

rows.label: dull-witted
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe being slow to grasp things and needing repeated explanation, so they are essentially the same concept, with slow-witted adding slow replies and dull-witted adding a slightly more general lack of sharpness.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe slowness of understanding, needing repeated explanation and lagging behind others; the labels are interchangeable.

rows.label: unaffected
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe staying composed under pressure without visible change in mood or judgment; unflappable emphasizes surprise and setbacks while unaffected also includes praise, but the core is the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe staying composed under external pressure without visible change. Unaffected stresses emotional imperviousness to praise and blame, while unflappable stresses not getting flustered by surprises and provocations, a near-identical concept with slight differences in emphasis.

rows.label: heretical
rows.sonnet_reason: Both mean holding views that depart from established doctrine; heterodox is slightly broader and more intellectual (not only religious, and treats accepted answers as one opinion among several), while heretical stresses openly maintaining religious departures.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean departing from established doctrine; heretical is the specifically religious, openly held form of the broader heterodox stance.

rows.label: gruff
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve saying things directly without softening, but gruff adds clipped, curt delivery and cutting pleasantries short, while blunt is just straightforward honesty without that brusque manner.
rows.opus_reason: Gruff, as described, includes unsoftened bluntness and adds a curt, clipped manner, so it is blunt directness with a narrower, rougher delivery.

rows.label: cheap
rows.sonnet_reason: Both mean spending as little as possible, but 'cheap' adds grudging, stingy resentment toward spending on others while 'frugal' is a neutral, prudent economy centered on need and making things last.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe minimizing spending to what is necessary; cheap is the same habit carried further, with grudging stinginess that extends to others.

rows.label: liberal
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve giving differing views a fair hearing; liberal adds tolerance of disagreement without hostility, while open-minded adds weighing views and willingness to change one's mind.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe giving opposing views a fair hearing. Liberal stresses tolerance toward those who disagree, while open-minded stresses being willing to change one's own mind, so the concept is the same with different emphasis.

rows.label: saturnine
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a habitually gloomy, brooding temperament with a negative outlook; saturnine adds a heavy, slow mood, while melancholic emphasizes sadness, so they differ only slightly in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a habitually gloomy, brooding temperament with a negative outlook; saturnine adds heaviness, melancholic stresses sadness, but they are essentially the same concept.

rows.label: overambitious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve setting high goals, but 'ambitious' is a drive to climb and achieve, while 'overambitious' adds unrealistic goals pursued despite plainly lacking the means; neither implies the other.
rows.opus_reason: Overambitious is ambition carried past realistic limits, the same reaching for high goals taken further, though ambitious stresses climbing in status.

rows.label: unmannered
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe rude behavior such as skipping courtesies and interrupting; the target adds blunt speech and the other adds a sharp tone and ignoring greetings, so they are essentially the same concept with slight differences in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe the same lack of courtesy: skipping please and thank you, interrupting, and speaking harshly. They can be used interchangeably.

rows.label: dog cheap
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve minimizing spending, but 'dog cheap' is an extreme, grudging stinginess that even costs the person, while 'frugal' is a sensible, often admirable thrift; same core, different degree and tone.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe minimizing spending, but dog cheap is an extreme, grudging version of frugality carried to self-defeating lengths.

rows.label: tenderminded
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe feeling others' pain and responding with care; tenderminded stresses compassion deciding one's actions and feeling others' pain as one's own, while compassionate is a slightly broader, less intense description of the same quality.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe empathic sensitivity and caring response to others' suffering; tenderminded emphasizes feeling others' pain as one's own and letting compassion govern behavior, a slightly stronger degree of the same concept.

rows.label: doltish
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve slow comprehension, but doltish adds saying foolish things unaware, while slow-witted adds delayed replies and needing repeated explanation; each has something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe slowness of comprehension, but doltish adds foolish talk and unawareness of one's own dimness, so it is the same quality with broader, more pejorative scope.

rows.label: stern
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve holding others to high standards without softness, but stern adds a severe, unsmiling demeanor while strict centers on demanding results and a philosophy of pushing people.
rows.opus_reason: Both centre on holding others to strict, exacting standards without softening. Stern adds the severe, unsmiling demeanour, while strict stresses the demanding stance itself.

rows.label: sensation-seeking
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve seeking novelty and thrill and disliking routine, but sensation-seeking stresses risk and intensity while adventurous stresses openness to the unfamiliar, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe chasing novelty and thrills and finding routine dull; sensation-seeking is essentially the same drive pushed further toward risk and intensity.

rows.label: oversensitive
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe taking offense easily at remarks or criticism; thin-skinned adds a stronger degree and the brooding or snapping reaction, so it is essentially the same concept with a difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe taking offense easily at remarks and criticism; thin-skinned adds a lasting reaction like brooding or snapping back, a slight difference of emphasis.

rows.label: foresightless
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe acting in the moment without planning ahead or weighing long-term consequences, so they are nearly the same concept, with slight differences in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe acting in the moment without planning or weighing future consequences; reactive adds an emphasis on responding to events as they arise, while foresightless stresses the missing foresight.

rows.label: saintly
rows.sonnet_reason: Forgiving is one component of the saintly description (forgiveness before it is asked), but saintly also includes patience under provocation and putting others first, so they overlap without either implying the other.
rows.opus_reason: Saintly includes pre-emptive forgiveness as one part of a broader package with patience and selflessness, so forgiving is a narrower piece of the same virtue.

rows.label: unpartisan
rows.sonnet_reason: Both mean not aligned with any party or faction; nonpartisan adds even-handed engagement with each side and judging on merits, a slight difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean not aligning with any political side; nonpartisan extends this to actively fair, merit-based judgment of each side's case.

rows.label: deeply involved
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe holding full attention on the task at hand until it is finished; 'focused' stresses resisting distractions while 'deeply involved' stresses absorption and also covers conversations.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe holding full attention on the task at hand until it is finished; focused stresses resisting distractions, while deeply involved stresses being absorbed, including in conversation.

rows.label: libidinous
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe strong, openly expressed sexual desire that colors conversation and how one views others, so they are near-synonyms with only slight differences in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe strong sexual appetite expressed in desire, talk and outlook toward others; they are essentially interchangeable.

rows.label: phlegmatic
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe staying composed under surprise and setbacks; phlegmatic adds unhurried, low-emotion temperament, while unflappable emphasizes not being visibly rattled, so they are near-synonyms with slight emphasis differences.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean staying composed and unflustered through setbacks and surprises, but phlegmatic adds a general unhurried temperament with little strong emotion shown at all.

rows.label: facetious
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve treating serious matters with inappropriate lightness, but facetious stresses joking and quipping while flippant stresses casual, dismissive disregard without requiring humor.
rows.opus_reason: Facetiousness is flippancy expressed specifically through jokes and quips, so it is a narrower, humour-focused form of the same inappropriate lightness toward serious matters.

rows.label: obtuse
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe being slow to grasp points and needing repeated explanation; slow-witted adds slow reply generation and is somewhat broader in scope.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe slowness in grasping explanations and needing repetition; slow-witted adds slow retorts but is essentially the same concept.

rows.label: inexplicit
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve communicating so that listeners must infer the meaning, but inexplicit is about hinting and leaving things unstated, while cryptic adds deliberate mystery and puzzle-like obscurity; neither implies the other.
rows.opus_reason: Cryptic is a stronger, deliberately puzzling form of leaving meaning unstated for the listener to infer, so it is the same concept carried further.

rows.label: satirical
rows.sonnet_reason: Both use mocking irony to expose folly and absurdity, but sardonic emphasizes a dry, cynical, biting tone while satirical emphasizes ridiculing pretension as a purposeful exposure, so they overlap heavily without being identical.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe ironic mockery that exposes folly and absurdity; sardonic mainly adds a drier, more cynical and biting tone.

rows.label: farsighted
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve prioritizing distant outcomes over immediate gains, but farsighted stresses foresight and planning ahead while long-term oriented stresses patient persistence and delayed payoff, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe orienting choices toward distant future outcomes. Farsighted stresses foresight and planning, while long-term oriented stresses patient persistence and deferring payoffs, a difference of emphasis.

rows.label: effervescent
rows.sonnet_reason: Both include bubbly warmth and cheer, but extraversion is broader, adding sociability, assertiveness, activity and excitement-seeking, while effervescent centers on bright, bubbly manner.
rows.opus_reason: Effervescence is the bubbly, cheerful-energy facet of extraversion, which is the broader trait that also covers assertiveness, activity and excitement-seeking, so the two differ mainly in scope.
